task.description: Idiom/scope gate on REQ-231 (Entities.Query.Cursor keyset-pagination codec + Entities.Query.FieldGrants default-deny field redaction) -- final requirement closing out the ISS-0438 entity-subsystem port (REQ-225-231). Independently re-verify compile/format/test, design fidelity, all 5 ACs' test coverage, the tenant_fixture_test.exs count bump, the Ecto.UUID.dump!/1 fix and its flagged robustness observation, scope discipline, OTP/Ecto idiom, migration idiom vs. precedent, broader regression, and whole-subsystem cohesion/open-question sanity.

result.note:
Own verification, all re-run fresh, not trusted from prior handoffs:

1. COMPILE/FORMAT/TEST: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> clean, no output. `mix format --check-formatted` -> clean, no output. `mix test test/letflow/entities/query_cursor_field_grants_test.exs --max-cases 1` -> 'Result: 8 passed', 0 failures.

2. DESIGN FIDELITY: `Letflow.Entities.Query.Cursor` (lib/letflow/entities/query/cursor.ex) and `Letflow.Entities.Query.FieldGrants` (lib/letflow/entities/query/field_grants.ex) match the CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved design exactly -- module names/namespace, `cursor_prefix/0` returning the literal "EQ:" (cursor.ex:60-64), the `"<prefix><mint_time_us>:<resume_key_json>"` raw payload with JSON array resume-key encoding (parse_resume_key_json/1, build_next_cursor/2), the row-wise lexicographic keyset comparison folded right-to-left via nested dynamic/2 (build_row_dynamic/1, matching design §2.3's formula), the implicit ascending `id` tiebreak, and FieldGrants' two-table default-deny-with-override model, sentinel `:__field_redacted__` (key retained, value replaced), and `load_restrictions/3`/`redact_field_values/2`/`redact_page/2` signatures all matching design §3.5 verbatim. Migrations' column/index shapes match design §3.2 exactly (entity_field_restrictions: id/entity_type/field_name/timestamps, unique index on (entity_type, field_name); user_entity_grants: id/user_id FK/entity_type/field_name/inserted_at-only, unique index on (user_id, entity_type, field_name)).

3. AC COVERAGE (test/letflow/entities/query_cursor_field_grants_test.exs, read in full): AC1 -- 'next_cursor round-trips through every page with no repeated or skipped records' (lines 182-239) uses a GENUINE multi-field, non-default sort (customer_name asc, age desc) against REQ-230's real Compiler.compile/2 and Allowlist.load/2, with 5 fixtures across 3 pages (2/2/1) and a uniqueness/count check on returned ids -- this is not the trivial default-sort case, confirmed by reading the request map at lines 203-209. A second test (241-257) covers the no-next-cursor case; a third (259-291) covers {:error, :resume_key_arity_mismatch} on a resent differently-shaped sort. AC2 -- 'a user with no matching grant has the restricted field redacted, key retained' (339-354) and 'a user holding an explicit grant sees the restricted field populated' (356-369), both against the same entity_field_restrictions row, exactly per the requirement's own 'two explicit tests' text; plus a redact_page/2 test (371-385) and a zero-restrictions-is-not-an-error test (387-395). AC3 is a design-doc property already verified by step-01b (§3.1 states the researched conclusion and names Letflow.Api.Authorization/Letflow.Secrets.Redaction as read) -- correctly not re-tested in code. AC4 -- structural test (404-414) asserting no lib/letflow/routers/**/*.ex references Query.Cursor/Query.FieldGrants, and independently confirmed via git diff --stat (below). AC5 -- confirmed by this review's own compile/format/test runs above.

4. tenant_fixture_test.exs BUMP: 41->43 confirmed correct (two new tables, entity_field_restrictions and user_entity_grants, both present in test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's @expected_tenant_tables, alphabetically placed). The updated comment at test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs:309-317 follows the file's own established running-history convention exactly (each requirement's bump appended to the same comment, old numbers preserved) -- same pattern REQ-226/228 already used.

5. Ecto.UUID.dump!/1 / recurring malformed-cursor-raise pattern: independently confirmed the fix is necessary and correctly scoped (maybe_dump/2, cursor.ex:353-356, applied only for :binary_id/Ecto.UUID typed comparisons). SECURITY-REVIEWER's flagged observation is legitimate: this is now the SECOND call site (after Letflow.Entities.Definitions.list_definitions/2's own precedent) where an unsigned, prefix-checked-only cursor's decoded component can reach Repo/Ecto without format validation and raise an unhandled ArgumentError on malformed input. A pattern recurring across two independent call sites, in the same subsystem family, is exactly the kind of finding that should become claimable follow-up work rather than a second silent one-off tolerance -- not a merge blocker (per-request isolation applies, no cross-tenant exposure, matches INV-8's own carve-out), but worth a proper hardening issue now that it is a pattern, not an instance. RECOMMENDATION TO ORCH: register a follow-up issue via letflow-queue (I did not self-assign a docs/issues/ISS-NNNN.yaml id myself, per ISSUE_QUEUE.md's explicit 'do not derive the id' rule -- that is ORCH's step) titled approximately 'Cursor-decoded components used in Repo calls without format validation raise unhandled exceptions on malformed input (list_definitions/2 and Query.Cursor)', severity MINOR-to-MODERATE (availability/DoS class, not data-exposure), tags [entities, cursor, robustness, unhandled-crash], suggesting a shared {:error, :invalid_cursor}-returning validation helper for :binary_id-typed resume/sort components instead of raising.

6. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: `git diff 80f650bc..HEAD --stat` shows exactly: 5 handoff jsons, the design doc, cursor.ex, field_grants.ex, the two new migrations, tenant_provisioning.ex (+4 lines, manifest registration only), the new test file, and tenant_fixture.ex/tenant_fixture_test.exs (both minimal, table-list/count additions only). No route, no controller, no unrelated file touched.

7. IDIOM: no unnecessary process machinery -- both new modules are pure functional/query-composition code, no GenServer/gen_statem misuse, consistent with this subsystem's row-based, transactional-context style (REQ-045's already-settled process-vs-row decision, not disturbed here). FieldGrants' schemaless Ecto query (from(x in "table_name", ...)) is a reasonable choice, not corner-cutting: the design (§3.5, §4 moduledoc) explicitly scopes this slice to the read-side loader/redactor only, defers the write path (and any schema modules it might need) to a future requirement, and the two tables have no application-level struct consumer today beyond the anti-join query itself -- introducing Ecto.Schema modules now, ahead of a write-path requirement that would actually use their changeset/validation machinery, would itself be the scope-creep this gate watches for. Correct call, not a shortcut.

8. MIGRATION IDIOM: both new migrations match the established tenant-scoped precedent exactly -- same header-comment structure (module doc comment, PLACEMENT/TENANT-SCOPED MIGRATION/INV-7 blocks) as REQ-226's/REQ-228's/ISS-0519's migrations, same mandatory `if prefix() do` guard, same registration discipline in Letflow.TenantProvisioning's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (verified: both new migrations registered, git diff shows exactly a 4-line addition), same primary_key: false / binary_id id / prefix: schema pattern.

9. BROADER REGRESSION (own run): `mix test test/letflow/entities/ --max-cases 1` -> 'Result: 137 passed'. `mix test test/letflow/api/ --max-cases 1` -> 'Result: 176 passed'. Both exactly match ELIXIR-DEV's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's reported figures; no stale tenant_template cache issue hit this run.

10. ISS-0438 WHOLE-SUBSYSTEM SANITY: Query.Cursor/Query.FieldGrants demonstrably compose with REQ-230's Compiler/Allowlist as one working pipeline -- the test file's own AC1 test calls Compiler.compile/2 and Allowlist.load/2 directly and feeds their output into Cursor.paginate/5, and AC2's tests exercise FieldGrants against real Records.create_record/2-produced rows, proving the full chain (Compiler -> Cursor -> FieldGrants) is genuinely usable together, not merely independently unit-tested. Grepped lib/letflow/design/req22*.md and req23*.md for OPEN QUESTION/OQ- markers: req225 §9 (cardinality-limit numbers, explicitly flagged as this design's own reasoned choice pending real R-Co source access -- non-blocking, informational), req226 §6 (three OQs, none touching REQ-231's scope), req227 §8 (four MINOR OQs on JSON-schema emission, unrelated to REQ-231), req228 §8 item 1 / req229 §7 item 2 (entity_def_version wire representation) -- this one chain genuinely passes an open question from REQ-228 to REQ-229 without full closure, but REQ-229 commits to a concrete working default (Base.decode16!/2, matching Letflow.Entities.Records.duplicate_result/1's existing decode) and explicitly flags where a future resolution would need to be updated -- this is a deliberately-deferred, non-silent, working-default note in this project's established design-doc style, not a silently-dropped question, and it is orthogonal to REQ-231's own scope (entity_def_version is opaque :typed_column metadata to Cursor, and is not JSON-field-restrictable so FieldGrants never touches it either). req230 §9 (three MINOR OQs on operator-set fidelity, JSONB :in composition, case-sensitivity) are all explicitly-scoped future-revisit notes with working defaults already shipped, none blocking. req231 itself has zero remaining open questions (§6: 'None remaining for this slice's own scope'), and its one deferred item (whether authoring a restriction/grant row needs a new Authorization permission) is correctly scoped to the not-yet-existing write-path requirement. No genuinely dangling, silently-dropped open question was found anywhere in the chain that should have blocked this close-out.

VERDICT: PASS. ISS-0438 (the entity-subsystem port, REQ-225 through REQ-231) is genuinely complete pending this merge -- every requirement in the chain shipped with its own SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER gate passes, the subsystem's pieces (Types/Allowlist/Compiler/Cursor/FieldGrants plus the earlier definitions/records/replay layer) compose and are demonstrated composing in real tests, no route/controller was ever added (correctly deferred throughout), and no open question in the design-doc chain was left silently unresolved -- every one still open is either non-blocking-and-flagged-for-future-revisit with a working default already shipped, or explicitly scoped to a not-yet-existing follow-on requirement. One non-blocking follow-up recommended above for ORCH to register through letflow-queue (the recurring unhandled-raise-on-malformed-cursor-component pattern, now at two call sites).
